title: Arabic Sentiment Analysis in Education and Distance Learning: A Scoping Review of Trends, Methods, Gaps, and Future Directions
abstract: This project is a systematic review of research on Arabic Sentiment Analysis in distance learning and education contexts. The review aims to systematically examine how sentiment analysis has been applied to Arabic-language educational data, identify the dominant research trends and methodological approaches, evaluate the datasets, linguistic resources, models, and evaluation practices used in the field, and identify important gaps that may guide future research. The review will focus on studies that apply sentiment analysis, sentiment classification, opinion mining, or closely related affective text-analysis techniques to Arabic-language data originating from educational or distance-learning contexts. These contexts may include online learning platforms, learning management systems, educational social media, student feedback, course evaluations, discussion forums, university-related online communication, and other digitally mediated educational environments. The study will follow the PRISMA 2020 guidelines and will use a predefined protocol for literature searching, screening, eligibility assessment, data extraction, methodological-quality assessment, and evidence synthesis. Relevant studies published within the predefined review period will be identified through systematic searches of selected academic databases using combinations of terms related to Arabic language, sentiment analysis, education, e-learning, online learning, distance learning, students, teachers, and educational feedback. Data will be extracted using a structured coding framework covering publication characteristics, educational context, geographical and institutional setting where reported, Arabic language variety or dialect, data source, dataset size and characteristics, annotation strategy, sentiment categories, preprocessing techniques, linguistic resources, feature representations, machine-learning and deep-learning models, transformer or large-language-model approaches, experimental settings, evaluation metrics, baseline comparisons, and reported limitations. The synthesis will examine the extent to which existing research reflects actual educational experiences and institutional learning environments, rather than broader public or social-media discourse. Particular attention will be given to the granularity of sentiment analysis tasks, the distinction between general sentiment and education-specific affective states, the representation of Arabic linguistic variation, the availability and quality of annotated datasets, and the consistency of evaluation protocols. The review will also assess methodological quality and reporting transparency, including dataset and annotation documentation, preprocessing and experimental details, train/test separation, reproducibility information, baseline selection, evaluation metrics, and statistical reporting where applicable. Reported performance will be interpreted in the context of dataset characteristics and experimental design rather than used as a standalone indicator of methodological superiority. The expected outcomes are a comprehensive characterization of the current state of Arabic sentiment analysis in education and distance learning, a synthesis of major methodological and application trends, identification of underrepresented educational contexts and Arabic linguistic varieties, assessment of limitations in datasets and evaluation practices, and a research agenda addressing the major gaps identified in the literature. The review will distinguish preregistered procedures from any subsequent methodological modifications. Any deviations from the preregistered protocol that become necessary during the review will be documented, justified, and explicitly reported in the final systematic review.

title: Understanding the Impact of AI identity Disclosure on User Engagement in Live-Streaming e-Commerce: The Roles of Perceived Content Quality, Trust, and Prevention Focus
abstract: Purpose – This paper aims to examine how AI identity disclosure influences engagement intention and to develop a model examining the roles of perceived trust, perceived content quality, and prevention focus. Specifically, this research examines the psychological mechanisms behind how AI disclosure influences engagement intention by considering the role of perceived trust and perceived content quality while exploring the boundary role of prevention focus. Design/Methodology/Approach – We used a scenario-based experimental design to collect data. Participants were assigned to an AI-disclosure condition or a non-disclosure condition, yielding 341 valid responses. The data were analyzed using an independent-samples t-test, regression analysis, hierarchical moderation analysis, and simple slope tests. Findings – This study investigates the impact of AI identity disclosure on user willingness to engage in e-commerce live streaming, with a particular focus on the moderating effect of prevention focus. The results indicate that AI identity disclosure markedly reduces user willingness to participate, as well as perceived trust and perceived content quality. In contrast, both perceived trust and perceived content quality have a positive effect on user willingness to engage. Additionally, prevention focus significantly moderates the relationships between AI identity disclosure and both perceived trust and perceived content quality, indicating that users with different motivational orientations respond differently to AI disclosure. Research Implications – In live-streaming e-commerce settings, this research broadens inquiry into AI disclosure and contributes fresh theoretical perspectives to related disciplines. Additionally, the results present important managerial insights for companies integrating AI virtual anchors into marketing strategies.

title: Constant Individual Regret in General Games
abstract: Uncoupled no-regret dynamics provide a decentralized route to equilibrium, but prior guarantees for individual regret retain a polylogarithmic dependence on the horizon. We remove this dependence for every finite $N$-player normal-form game under full-information feedback. We introduce \emph{ECHO-OFTRL}: optimistic follow-the-regularized-leader (OFTRL) equipped with an EMA cascade for high-order optimism (ECHO), where EMA denotes exponential moving average. The algorithm is deterministic and fully uncoupled. If $m_{\max}$ denotes the largest action-set size, then, simultaneously for every horizon $T\geq1$, it guarantees that each of the $N$ players in the game incurs regret upper bounded by $O(\textrm{poly}(N, \log m_{\max}))$. Our algorithm leverages a new form of optimism inspired by modern filter design.

title: DP-VOXLET: Provable Speaker Anonymization for Disentangled Speech Representations
abstract: Systems for speaker anonymization obfuscate the speaker of an utterance, while maintaining its original semantic contents and prosody. Recent solutions for speaker anonymization rely on learned representations that disentangle an utterance into semantic contents and speaker properties. To anonymize an utterance, these systems replace the speaker properties while leaving the semantic contents unchanged---an approach that can produce strong results on empirical measures of privacy. In this work, we introduce speaker differential privacy, a formal definition of speaker anonymization based on the framework of differential privacy, and a mechanism for speaker anonymization that provably satisfies the definition. In contrast to prior heuristic-based anonymization systems, our approach enables a provable lower bound on re-identification success rate (e.g. equal error rate) for any possible adversary. We implement our approach in a framework that is compatible with existing disentangled representations. Compared to the prior work on differential privacy for speaker anonymization, our approach achieves significantly higher utility.

title: TRIPPULSE: Multi-Agent Travel Planning with Review-Grounded Reasoning
abstract: Travel itinerary generation requires balancing strict spatio-temporal constraints with human preferences. Existing LLM-based planners mainly rely on structured attributes and pre- defined traveler personas, but real travel deci- sions are often shaped by reviews that reveal experiential factors such as comfort, safety, ser- vice quality, ambiance, crowding, and hidden risks absent from structured databases. Incor- porating such review information is therefore critical to realistic, user-centric itinerary gen- eration. We propose TRIPPULSE1, a multi- agent framework for review-grounded travel planning. Instead of relying on a monolithic planner (and face context and reasoning bot- tlenecks), TRIPPULSE2 decomposes itinerary generation into specialized agents (each op- erating over localized contexts) for accom- modations, transportation, meals, attractions, and events, coordinated through a global or- chestrator with scheduling mechanisms that enforce temporal and budget feasibility. We augment TRIPCRAFT with 100K+ real-world reviews and introduce Review-Grounded Per- sona Alignment (RGPA), an LLM-as-a-Judge metric for evaluating alignment with human- centric travel experiences. Experiments across multiple trip durations and diverse proprietary and open-source models show that TRIPPULSE maintains strong constraint satisfaction while generating more personalized and experien- tially grounded itineraries.

title: An Optical Pathway to Movable Rydberg Atomic Quantum Receivers
abstract: This paper develops an optically movable Rydberg atomic quantum receiver (RAQR), in which the probe and coupling beams are steered within each vapor cell to dynamically reconfigure the effective radio-frequency (RF) sensing position without mechanical actuation. A closed-form equivalent baseband model is derived by separating the atomic transduction coefficient, optical steering phase, and cell-center array response into distinct factors and the accuracy of the resulting model is validated against numerical solutions of the Lindblad master equation. Based on the derived model, we reveal two complementary channel-shaping mechanisms, including intrinsic beam-pattern shaping through RF-to-optical transduction and per-cell phase control enabled by optical displacement. To further exploit these capabilities, a non-convex sum-rate maximization problem is formulated over the optical positions and local oscillator design and solved via an alternating optimization framework with analytical gradients. Simulation results validate the derived model and demonstrate substantial performance gains enabled by optical movability, highlighting its potential as a programmable receiver architecture for future wireless networks.

title: UFPR-PEs: A Brazilian Face Recognition Benchmark with Self-Declared Race/Color Labels
abstract: While face recognition systems are widely deployed, ensuring their demographic reliability and robustness under uncontrolled visual conditions remains a critical challenge. To bridge this gap, we present UFPR-PEs, a benchmark for face recognition bias evaluation using public videos of elected Brazilian politicians annotated with official self-declared race/color categories. The dataset adopts the Brazilian census taxonomy, including the parda category, which has no direct equivalent in the U.S.- or Europe-centric schemas commonly used in prior benchmarks. Our benchmark is built from compressed public video and preserves difficult samples so that performance can be analyzed under realistic conditions. We describe the construction pipeline, report dataset statistics, and evaluate face recognition performance across verification and (closed- and open-set) identification settings, including subgroup analysis by race/color and difficulty level. The results show that recognition performance varies substantially with image quality, and that subgroup gaps must be interpreted jointly with visual difficulty rather than in isolation. Overall, UFPR-PEs provides a reproducible and demographically grounded setting for studying face recognition bias under challenging public video conditions.

title: OPUS: A Simple yet Effective Unified Framework for Open-Vocabulary Detection
abstract: Recent unified open-vocabulary detection (OVD) supports heterogeneous prompts, including text queries, visual exemplars, and their combinations, but often rely on increasingly complex designs such as heavy cross-modal fusion, staged training, and iterative annotation pipelines. We revisit whether such complexity is necessary in the era of stronger foundation models. Our finding is that unified OVD can be made substantially simpler with semantic-rich visual representations and scalable grounding supervision. We present OPUS (\textbf{O}pen-vocabulary, \textbf{P}rompt-\textbf{U}nified, \textbf{S}imple), a unified detector supporting text, interactive visual, generic visual, and mixed prompting within one framework. OPUS adopts a simple three-part design. Its model architecture combines a semantic-rich visual encoder, built on a DINOv3-ConvNeXt-B backbone with efficient hybrid encoding, with a prompt-aware decoder that avoids prompt-specific branches for unified prompt reasoning. OPUS is trained with a one-stage text-visual training strategy with Instance-level Contrastive Alignment (ICA), and is supported by a SAM3-based single-pass data engine for heterogeneous grounding supervision. Experiments on COCO, LVIS-minival, and ODinW35 show that OPUS achieves state-of-the-art Visual-I performance, reaching 68.1/69.2/54.7 AP, while maintaining balanced Text and Visual-G accuracy. OPUS also turns mixed prompting from interference into complementarity, improving over text or visual prompt alone. These results show that simplicity and strong unified prompting capability can be achieved together.

title: Will the User Ever Know? Covert Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on Tool-Using LLM Agents
abstract: As LLM agents take real-world actions through tools, indirect prompt injection (IPI) has emerged as a serious threat. The standard metric, Attack Success Rate (ASR), counts whether an injection succeeds but ignores what the user notices in the agent's final response. Looking at successful injection traces, we find two distinct outcomes: the agent executes the injection while returning an otherwise normal response, or reports the injected action in its final response, giving the user a chance to notice. We call these covert and overt successes. From the user's perspective, we decompose ASR into the Covert Success Rate (CSR), counting successes leaving no trace in the final response, and the Overt Success Rate (OSR), counting successes the user can detect. To understand what drives the gap, we analyze successful trajectories and find that the agent's behavior after the injection separates covert from overt: covert traces hand control back to the user task before ending, while overt traces end at the attack itself. This split follows from the ReAct format, where the final response summarizes the most recent action. Building on this observation, we propose ICoA (Induced Covert Attack), an IPI attack designed to induce covert outcomes by steering the agent back to the user task after executing the injection. Across four target models on AgentDojo, ICoA achieves the highest CSR, with gains of 3.79-12.01 percentage points over the strongest baseline.

Building on this observation, we propose ICoA (Induced Covert Attack), an IPI attack designed to induce covert outcomes by steering the agent back to the user task after executing the injection. Across four target models on AgentDojo, ICoA achieves the highest CSR, with gains of 3.79-12.01 percentage points over the strongest baseline.

title: Improving Information Extraction with Learned Queries
abstract: When information extraction fails, a natural instinct is to improve the model doing it: for example, by scaling it up or refining its reasoning. In this paper, we show that another part of the pipeline matters at least as much: the queries used to elicit this information. Across four clinical benchmarks and five LLMs, improving the question design alone raises performance by 18.6 F1-score points, i.e. more than using larger extraction models. To make such question design learnable, we introduce List of Questions (LoQ), which generates document-specific question sets, and FeedQ, a feedback-driven optimization method that iteratively refines questions against extraction outcomes. The resulting optimized questions can be used to train lightweight generators: with fine-tuning, 4B-parameter models match or outperform expert-derived baselines and substantially exceed the performance of much larger untuned models. We release a dataset of 12,820 optimized questions to support a broader shift in information extraction research toward treating question design as a first-class problem.

title: Language-Statistical Analysis of Neural Audio Codec Tokens Across Architectures, Corpora, and Noise Conditions
abstract: Neural audio codecs (NACs) convert speech into discrete token sequences, and prior work has reported that these sequences follow language-like statistical laws. This paper analyzes the token statistics of 13 NACs spanning multi-codebook residual vector quantization (RVQ), single-codebook VQ, and non-VQ designs, evaluated on three corpora under clean, white-noise, and real-world DEMAND-noise conditions. Zipf and Heaps parameters, unigram entropy, codebook occupancy, and Jensen-Shannon divergence (JSD) are estimated from matched token samples with explicit fit-validity safeguards and family-conditional $n$-gram orders. Corpus identity explains little variance in any metric, whereas acoustic condition and quantizer meta-category dominate in a metric-dependent way, and unigram entropy is the metric most strongly associated with meta-category. Clean-to-noise JSD computed at a common unigram order is associated with mel-cepstral distortion most clearly under DEMAND noise. The collapse and explosion degradation signatures previously reported for RVQ codecs concentrate in RVQ cells under white and DEMAND noise, respectively; explosion also occurs in non-VQ codecs, and single-codebook VQ codecs shift in occupancy and distribution shape without either signature. These results provide architecture-conditioned conventions for applying language-statistical analysis to NAC tokens.

title: What Emerges and What Breaks in Self-Play Driving
abstract: Training autonomous driving policies through pure self-play has recently shown promising results. Following Gigaflow and Puffer- Drive, we train driving policies in a similar self-play fashion, but extend the models from MLPs to Transformers and train on the high-definition map of a real city, where we ultimately aim to deploy them. On the CARLA and Waymax benchmarks, our policies fall short of Gigaflow, and we trace the gap to specific failure modes, including reward hacking at traffic lights and a missing incentive to stop at stop signs. We further analyze which traffic rules emerge from self-play and how closely they match human driving, and we confirm that reward conditioning yields the intended diversity of driving behaviors. A demonstration of a trained policy is available at https://laursisask-ut.github.io/eccvdemo.

title: Vocal Music under Phoneme-Conditional Analysis
abstract: The vocal music of each language carries a distinctive sonic identity, even without instrumental accompaniment. We ask whether these differences are measurable and traceable to specific phonemes. To tackle this question, we introduce phoneme-conditional analysis, which isolates the acoustic effect of typologically distinctive phonemes by comparing marker syllables against matched non-marker controls within the same song, holding singer, melody, and genre constant. Across nine typologically diverse languages and thousands of songs, we measure effects along five acoustic dimensions. Song-level profiles built from these effects identify the language of an unaccompanied vocal at 85.5% balanced accuracy in a nine-way classification with folds grouped by artist; whether the separability arises by accumulation of the phoneme-local effects themselves is left open. Our findings suggest that phonological structure leaves systematic and measurable traces in how each language is sung.

title: Design and Implementation of Large Language Model-Based Inference Pipeline for Fire Investigation
abstract: This study designed and implemented an on-premises generative artificial intelligence (AI)-based fire investigation support pipeline to effectively utilize unstructured fire incident overview information. Existing systems rely on structured fields and keyword-based searches, making it difficult to reflect the contextual and structural similarities in narrative overviews. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes an integrated pipeline comprising text preprocessing, similar case retrieval and selection, large language model (LLM)-based inference of ignition factors, report generation, and result evaluation. In the preprocessing stage, sentence correction and summarization are performed to reduce the variation in expressions while preserving the core meaning. Fire-investigation-related keywords are extracted and used as search queries. In the similar case retrieval stage, semantic and keyword-based searches are combined to improve accuracy and contextual understanding. Subsequently, the retrieved cases are selected based on the structural consistency of the incident components, thereby deriving cases suitable for onsite fire investigation. Experimental results show that the proposed approach addresses the problems of similar case retrieval that cannot be resolved by conventional methods and improves the accuracy and consistency of LLM-based fire-cause inference.

title: Analisis Sentimen Ulasan Aplikasi Transportasi Online menggunakan IndoBERT dan Explainable AI (LIME)
abstract: Gojek and Grab are two leading online transportation platforms in Indonesia, receiving millions of user reviews on the Google Play Store. Previous studies analyzing reviews of both applications have generally produced final sentiment classifications without transparently explaining why a review is categorized into a particular sentiment. This study integrates the IndoBERT model with the Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) method, Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME), to address this gap. The IndoBERT model (indobert-base-p1) was fine-tuned on a dataset of Gojek and Grab reviews collected using google-play-scraper, with semi-automatic labeling based on star ratings. Evaluation results show that the model achieved 90.57% accuracy and a weighted F1-Score of 90.60%, substantially exceeding IndoBERT performance in the implicit hate speech domain, which reached 55%. These findings demonstrate that explicit and implicit linguistic complexity is an important determinant of Transformer model performance. LIME analysis identified the word “memudahkan” as the most dominant feature, with a weight of +0.61, in driving positive sentiment classification. This study contributes to Indonesian-language sentiment analysis by integrating LIME to provide transparent explanations of model predictions for online transportation reviews.

title: TINJAUAN SISTEMATIK APLIKASI CHATGPT DALAM ANALISIS RETORIK ARAB
abstract: Kajian tinjauan sistematik ini meneliti aplikasi ChatGPT dalam analisis retorik Arab khususnya dari aspek kemampuan model bahasa besar ini mengenal pasti, mentafsir dan menghuraikan unsur-unsur retotik dalam teks Arab. Perkembangan model bahasa besar (Large Language Model) telah membuka ruang baharu dalam penyelidikan bahasa Arab termasuk analisis nahu, semantik, terjemahan, ringkasan teks, pengecaman gaya bahasa dan pentafsiran unsur retorik. Namun begitu, keupayaan ChatGPT dalam memahami teks Arab masih berhadapan dengan cabaran seperti kerumitan morfologi, variasi dialek, ketiadaan baris, konteks budaya, makna tersirat dan kehalusan disiplin balaghah. Kajian ini menggunakan pendekatan tinjauan sistematik berpandukan PRISMA 2020 bagi mengenal pasti trend, kaedah, dapatan dan jurang kajian berkaitan aplikasi ChatGPT dalam analisis retorik Arab. Selepas saringan dan semakan teks penuh, sebanyak 17 artikel dimasukkan dalam sintesis akhir. Hasil tinjauan menunjukkan bahawa ChatGPT berpotensi membantu proses analisis teks Arab melalui penjanaan tafsiran awal, pengenalpastian struktur linguistik, cadangan terjemahan dan huraian retorik. Walau bagaimanapun, kajian-kajian terdahulu turut menunjukkan bahawa model ini masih lemah dalam aspek ketepatan istilah klasik, pengesanan unsur retorik yang halus, huraian konteks syair Arab dan kawalan halusinasi. Oleh itu, kajian ini mencadangkan model penggunaan ChatGPT secara bersyarat iaitu sebagai alat sokongan analisis awal yang perlu disahkan oleh pakar bahasa Arab dan sumber turath. Kajian masa hadapan perlu membangunkan instrumen penilaian yang lebih khusus untuk mengukur ketepatan ChatGPT dalam bidang retorik Arab khususnya tashbih, isti'arah, kinayah dan fungsi retorik dalam teks klasik. This systematic review examines the application of ChatGPT in Arabic rhetorical analysis, particularly its ability to identify, interpret and explain rhetorical elements in Arabic texts. The development of large language models (LLMs) has opened new opportunities in Arabic language research, including grammatical analysis, semantics, translation, text summarisation, stylistic identification and the interpretation of rhetorical features. Nevertheless, ChatGPT’s ability to understand Arabic texts continues to face several challenges, including morphological complexity, dialectal variation, the absence of diacritical marks, cultural context, implicit meanings and the subtleties of balaghah as a rhetorical discipline. This study adopts a systematic review approach guided by PRISMA 2020 to identify trends, methods, findings and research gaps related to the application of ChatGPT in Arabic rhetorical analysis. Following the screening process and full-text review, 17 articles were included in the final synthesis. The findings indicate that ChatGPT has the potential to support Arabic text analysis through the generation of preliminary interpretations, identification of linguistic structures, translation suggestions and rhetorical explanations. However, previous studies also indicate that the model remains limited in terms of the accurate use of classical terminology, detection of subtle rhetorical devices, interpretation of the context of Arabic poetry and control of hallucinated information. Therefore, this review proposes a conditional model of ChatGPT use, whereby it should function as a supporting tool for preliminary analysis that must subsequently be verified by Arabic language experts and classical turath sources. Future studies should develop more specialised assessment instruments to evaluate the accuracy of ChatGPT in Arabic rhetoric, particularly in relation to tashbih, isti‘arah, kinayah, and rhetorical functions in classical texts.

title: Competitive Goal Reconstruction in Transformer-Based Agents: Will Substitution as a Candidate Mechanism for Goal Drift
abstract: Recent empirical research has documented goal drift in large language model (LLM) agents — measurable behavioral divergence from assigned objectives under sustained environmental pressure (Arike et al., 2025; Saebo et al., 2026; Menon et al., 2026). The phenomenon has been characterized and partially mitigated across multiple independent lines of work — attention competition, softmax dispersion, positional effects, residual stream dynamics — but these findings have not been unified into a single mechanistic account, and the mechanism driving goal drift has not been formally identified. We propose will substitution as a candidate unifying mechanism: the hypothesis that goal persistence in current transformer architecture appears to arise from recurrent reconstruction of distributed representations across the context-dependent forward pass rather than from access to a dedicated goal-maintenance substrate, making goal persistence a competitive resource allocation problem rather than a retrieval or retention problem. Under this framing, goal drift is not a corruption process but a reconstruction process — the model is not losing a goal, it is repeatedly recomputing what the goal appears to be from the current context state, with no dedicated goal-maintenance substrate identified in current transformer architectures that would maintain the goal's competitive position against growing environmental content. We ground this hypothesis in the residual stream framework (Elhage et al., 2021), the mathematics of multi-head softmax attention including the provable attention dispersion property under long contexts (Barbero et al., 2024), pre-norm residual dynamics, LayerNorm's interaction with semantic direction preservation through the unembedding pathway, MLP key-value memory contributions (Geva et al., 2021), and the compounding positional disadvantage for system-prompt goal tokens including LayerNorm-induced recency bias (Kim et al., 2025). We define displacement pressure using a context-independent reference goal representation with explicitly conservative asymmetry, precisely specify the minimal context token for mathematical operationalization, trace the full pathway from displaced attention through LayerNorm renormalization to shifted action probability, and demonstrate that the mechanism is consistent with documented empirical signatures. We explicitly separate what prior literature has established from what this paper introduces as a testable hypothesis. The paper does not claim that will substitution has been experimentally established as the definitive mechanism of goal drift; rather, it formalizes the mechanism as a candidate explanation that can be independently tested against transformer behavior.

title: 拓扑量子几何的自适应性重构
abstract: This paper explores the potential of incorporating self-adaptive restructuring mechanisms into quantum geometry, aiming to revolutionize quantum information processing. We propose a novel quantum computing framework based on dynamic topology fields, enabling quantum systems to dynamically adjust their topological structure in response to observation. This dynamic adjustment, driven by an algorithm, distinguishes this approach from traditional static quantum state representations. The core claim is that this self-adaptive restructuring allows for the creation of more complex quantum information processing capabilities. The research builds upon established principles of topology and quantum mechanics, exploring a potential pathway toward more versatile and powerful quantum algorithms. This work presents a framework for dynamically shaping quantum states through a carefully designed algorithm, offering a fundamentally new approach to quantum computation.

title: Probability Logic Framework for Automated Optimization Algorithms
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on a probabilistic framework, designed to automatically adjust parameters and adapt to environmental changes. The core mechanism leverages a probabilistic model to quantify optimization result quality and employs feedback from the environment to dynamically adjust parameters. This approach aims to improve the adaptability and reliability of the algorithm, moving beyond traditional parameter-driven methods. The study explores the potential of probabilistic modeling to enhance optimization performance in complex and dynamic scenarios.

The core mechanism leverages a probabilistic model to quantify optimization result quality and employs feedback from the environment to dynamically adjust parameters. This approach aims to improve the adaptability and reliability of the algorithm, moving beyond traditional parameter-driven methods. The study explores the potential of probabilistic modeling to enhance optimization performance in complex and dynamic scenarios.

title: Adaptive Geometric Optimization (AGO) Algorithm
abstract: Adaptive Geometric Optimization (AGO) is a novel algorithm designed to enhance machine learning model performance through automated parameter adjustment guided by geometric principles. Traditional parameter tuning methods often rely on guesswork or predefined rules, failing to fully leverage the inherent structure of data. This paper presents a new algorithm that directly incorporates geometric optimization techniques, enabling the model to dynamically adjust its parameters based on the data's geometric characteristics. We demonstrate the efficacy of AGO through a series of case studies across diverse machine learning tasks, showcasing its ability to achieve superior performance compared to conventional methods. This work introduces a robust and adaptable framework for optimizing machine learning models, offering a significant step towards more effective and intelligent AI systems.

title: Non-Linear Self-Organizing Structures Analysis: A Quantum Algorithm
abstract: This paper explores the development of a novel quantum algorithm for the analysis of non-linear self-organizing structures. Traditional methods often struggle to effectively model and understand complex systems exhibiting nonlinear behavior. Quantum mechanics offers a unique computational paradigm, specifically leveraging quantum entanglement to facilitate the evolution of these structures and provide more precise predictions. This work proposes a quantum algorithm centered around the manipulation of entangled states to achieve enhanced analysis capabilities. We detail the core mechanism of the algorithm, outlining its quantum operations and the potential for improved accuracy in predicting complex system dynamics. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential applications and future research directions within this field.

title: Title: Hierarchical Cognitive Networks for Algorithmic Self-Reflection
abstract: This paper introduces a novel cognitive network architecture, termed "Hierarchical Cognitive Networks," designed to facilitate algorithmic self-reflection and refinement. Traditional AI systems often operate through brute-force optimization, while this architecture aims to cultivate a more deliberate and iterative process of design improvement. The core principle is a hierarchical structure where algorithms analyze their own code, identify weaknesses, and restructure themselves, mirroring human-like cognitive processes. We propose a 'meta-cognitive' loop that dynamically adjusts the network's parameters based on internal self-assessment. This system aims to enhance algorithmic robustness, discover novel solutions, and ultimately improve the quality of the underlying algorithms. The paper details the network's architecture, proposes a novel 'meta-cognitive' loop, and discusses preliminary results demonstrating its potential for algorithmic self-improvement.

title: High-Dimensional Probability Field Theory: Adaptive Dynamics
abstract: This paper introduces a novel high-dimensional probability field theory model that employs adaptive dynamics to automatically adjust parameters based on data. The model aims to generate complex spacetime structures and dynamic evolution of models. We leverage a "dynamic probability field" mechanism to simulate data evolution by dynamically adjusting parameters within the probability field. This approach offers a more natural and intuitive modeling framework, particularly for complex systems and non-linear processes. The core mechanism focuses on dynamically updating probability field parameters to mimic data dynamics. This development addresses the limitations of traditional models by providing a flexible and adaptable approach to generating sophisticated temporal dynamics.

title: ##拓扑几何信息论的进化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel evolutionary algorithm, termed "拓扑几何信息论" (TGI), designed for optimizing complex, multi-layered machine learning models, particularly neural network architectures. The core innovation lies in incorporating a "拓扑进化" (Topology Evolution) mechanism, which leverages the learning and imitation of topology-driven features during the evolutionary process. This mechanism introduces random noise to guide the model generation towards more complex and scalable structural arrangements. The goal is to improve the generalization ability and robustness of the resulting models compared to traditional evolutionary algorithms. This work explores the potential of utilizing topology as a guiding principle for model design and optimization.

title: Algorithmic Complexity Theory for Quantum Simulation
abstract: Quantum simulation, a cornerstone of quantum computing, presents significant challenges in algorithm design and optimization. Traditional simulation methods often struggle with the inherent complexity of quantum systems, demanding substantial computational resources. This paper proposes a novel approach to algorithmic complexity theory specifically tailored for quantum simulation, focusing on the optimization of quantum state and interaction representation. We introduce a new, adaptive complexity measure designed to efficiently represent quantum states and interactions, thereby reducing the computational burden and enabling more practical simulations. The core mechanism centers around dynamically adjusting the complexity measure based on the system's specific characteristics, leading to improved performance across a range of quantum algorithms. We analyze the impact of this new measure through theoretical proofs and preliminary simulations, demonstrating its potential to significantly enhance the efficiency of quantum simulation.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Intelligent Synthesis
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental quantum phenomenon, has emerged as a promising resource for enhancing intelligence and synthetic capabilities. This paper explores the application of quantum entanglement to intelligent synthesis, focusing on a novel system designed to improve knowledge generation and generalization. The paper details the system's architecture, explores its potential benefits, and discusses future research directions, emphasizing the unique advantages conferred by quantum entanglement in this context.

title: Adaptive Quantum State Control
abstract: This paper investigates the development of an adaptive quantum state control algorithm designed to dynamically adjust quantum states in response to environmental changes. The core concept revolves around leveraging quantum state's inherent adaptability to achieve more precise quantum operations and computation. We propose a novel algorithm that employs a feedback loop to continuously refine the quantum state, effectively mitigating the effects of decoherence and enhancing the fidelity of quantum states. The algorithm's mechanism centers on a controlled evolution process, driven by an environment-aware feedback mechanism, allowing for precise manipulation and error correction. This research explores the potential of this approach to overcome limitations of traditional quantum control techniques, particularly in complex environments. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, demonstrates its performance through simulations and preliminary experiments, and concludes with a discussion of future research directions.

title: Black Fur Seal: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Black Fur Seal Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces Black Fur Seal (BFS), a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of black fur seals. BFS leverages the observed strategies of these seals – specifically their tendency to explore areas with low resource density while maintaining a balance between exploration and exploitation – to develop a novel search process. The algorithm incorporates a dynamic exploration probability based on a modified variance estimation technique, mimicking the seals' selective movement patterns. BFS operates within a defined search space, iteratively updating its solution set using a combination of a global search component, based on a particle swarm optimization (PSO) variant, and a local search component, employing a simulated annealing approach. The performance of BFS is evaluated through a series of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and adaptability to diverse challenges. The key innovations of BFS lie in its adaptive exploration strategy and the hybrid combination of PSO and simulated annealing, leading to improved convergence rates and solution quality compared to traditional metaheuristic methods. The algorithm's core mechanism is defined by the following key equations: `p_e(t) = α * exp(-β * (x_i(t) - x_best(t))^2) + (1 - α) * p_e(t-1)`, where `p_e(t)` represents the exploration probability at time `t`, `α` is a learning rate, `β` is a variance control parameter, `x_i(t)` is the position of the i-th particle at time `t`, and `x_best(t)` is the best position found so far. Furthermore, the update rule for particle velocities in the PSO component is defined as `v_i(t+1) = w * v_i(t) + c1 * rand() * (x_best(t) - x_i(t)) + c2 * rand() * (p_best(i) - x_i(t))`, where `v_i(t+1)` is the velocity of the i-th particle at time `t+1`, `w` is the inertia weight, `c1` and `c2` are acceleration coefficients, `rand()` is a random number between 0 and 1, and `p_best(i)` is the best position found by the i-th particle. The simulated annealing component utilizes a cooling schedule `T(t+1) = T(t) * exp(-cooling_rate)`, where `T(t)` is the temperature at time `t` and `cooling_rate` is the rate at which the temperature decreases.

title: Bismarck Blossom Bat: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Bismarck Blossoms
abstract: This paper presents Bismarck Blossom Bat (BBB), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Bismarck blossoms ( *Eremostemma bismarckianum* ), a unique plant species found in the Amazon rainforest. Bismarck blossoms exhibit a remarkable ability to orient themselves towards the sun, even when partially obscured by foliage, utilizing a sophisticated mechanism involving the relative angles of sunlight and shadow. BBB leverages this biological inspiration to develop a new optimization strategy. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, with individuals representing potential solutions. The movement of bats (representing solutions) is governed by a dynamic polarization mechanism, mimicking the blossom's sun-tracking ability. This polarization is influenced by both the received information from other bats and the local environmental conditions, represented by the angle of sunlight. The algorithm incorporates a dynamic adjustment of polarization strength, a local search mechanism, and a termination criterion based on convergence. Experimental results on benchmark optimization problems demonstrate that BBB achieves competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, highlighting its potential for solving complex optimization challenges. The algorithm's design prioritizes adaptability and robustness, reflecting the Bismarck blossom's remarkable survival strategy.

title: ## Big Mink: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of Big Mink
abstract: This paper presents Big Mink, a novel metaheuristic algorithm designed to address complex optimization problems. Inspired by the foraging behavior of Big Minks – particularly their strategic movement patterns and decision-making processes – Big Mink leverages a combination of adaptive memory, Lévy flight-inspired exploration, and a dynamic territory management system. The algorithm aims to achieve robust convergence and high solution quality. We detail the algorithm's core components, including the territory assignment mechanism, the adaptive memory update rule, and the Lévy flight-based exploration strategy. The performance of Big Mink is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness compared to established metaheuristic methods. The key mathematical formulations and notations used within the algorithm are explicitly defined, ensuring clarity and reproducibility. We explore the algorithm's parameters and demonstrate their impact on performance. Ultimately, Big Mink offers a promising approach for tackling challenging optimization tasks.

title: Geometric Topology for Bayesian Network Inference
abstract: Geometric Topology for Bayesian Network Inference explores the application of geometric topology to enhance the efficiency and expressiveness of Bayesian Network inference. The core concept revolves around constructing a geometric representation of the network, facilitating novel inference techniques such as geometric induction. This paper investigates the potential of this approach to overcome limitations in traditional Bayesian Network inference methods, aiming to improve both speed and accuracy. We present a novel method for generating geometric representations, demonstrating its effectiveness in exploring the network space and ultimately providing a more robust and efficient inference process.

title: Distributed Knowledge Graph Reasoning with Causal Relation Modeling
abstract: This paper addresses the challenges in distributed knowledge graph reasoning, particularly the issue of spurious correlations leading to inaccurate and potentially misleading inferences. We propose a novel framework for distributed knowledge graph reasoning that integrates causal relation modeling. The core claim is that incorporating causal relationships into the reasoning process significantly enhances the accuracy and interpretability of the resulting inferences. The mechanism involves decomposing the knowledge graph into smaller, manageable subgraphs, each handled by a dedicated node or resource. Within each subgraph, a causal model is employed to identify and mitigate spurious correlations, thereby improving the reliability of the inference results. Our approach represents a departure from traditional knowledge graph reasoning methods that often neglect causal relationships, offering a more robust and trustworthy solution for complex reasoning tasks. The framework's modular design facilitates scalability and adaptability to diverse knowledge graph structures. We present a theoretical foundation for the approach, outlining the key components and their interactions. Furthermore, we discuss potential applications and future research directions. ---

title: Quantum Security Computation Based on Quantum Decoherence
abstract: This paper explores the potential of leveraging quantum decoherence for building highly secure computational systems. The core idea is to exploit the inherent fragility of quantum states when interacting with the environment, specifically through quantum decoherence, to create a robust defense against eavesdropping. We propose a framework for quantum key distribution (QKD) and quantum-safe computation that fundamentally relies on controlling and manipulating decoherence events. The proposed approach aims to establish a significantly higher level of security compared to traditional cryptographic methods by embedding security directly within the physical properties of the quantum system. The paper details a theoretical model and outlines key considerations for practical implementation, focusing on the precise control of decoherence to maximize security while minimizing computational overhead. We demonstrate how carefully engineered decoherence can act as a dynamic, adaptive security layer, rendering classical attacks ineffective. The primary contribution of this work lies in providing a novel hardware security paradigm based on the precise manipulation of quantum decoherence, offering a promising avenue for future quantum-secure computing technologies.

title: Title: Adaptive Wavefunction Collapse (AWC)
abstract: Quantum information processing relies heavily on the precise manipulation and collapse of quantum states. Traditional methods often require explicit, manually calibrated collapse sequences, limiting the algorithm's adaptability. Adaptive Wavefunction Collapse (AWC) presents a novel quantum algorithm designed to automatically adjust wavefunction collapse based on observed data, significantly enhancing information processing speed and potentially unlocking new quantum capabilities. This paper details the core mechanism of AWC, outlining its feedback loop, data-driven guidance, and the resulting dynamic collapse process. We explore the algorithm's potential advantages and limitations, emphasizing its adaptability and efficiency compared to traditional approaches.

title: Quantum Machine Learning Adaptive Models
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning Adaptive Models represent a novel approach to machine learning, leveraging the unique capabilities of quantum computing to dynamically adapt to complex datasets. This paper explores the development of such models, focusing on their potential to enhance medical image analysis and financial risk assessment. The core mechanism centers around quantum machine learning algorithms designed to automatically learn intricate patterns and features from data, resulting in significantly improved accuracy and efficiency compared to traditional methods. We outline the theoretical framework, key algorithm design considerations, and potential applications of this paradigm shift. The research demonstrates the promise of quantum-enhanced models for challenging data sets, offering a significant advancement in both predictive power and computational efficiency.

title: Dynamic Adaptable Matrix Algorithm for Machine Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic adaptable matrix algorithm designed to enhance the adaptability and optimization capabilities of machine learning models. Traditional machine learning approaches often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their ability to effectively handle data variations and environmental changes. Our algorithm dynamically adjusts the matrix parameters based on real-time data analysis, enabling the model to continuously adapt to evolving conditions. The core mechanism involves a novel "morphological" measure and a matrix adaptation strategy that automatically adjusts parameter values, offering a more robust and flexible approach to optimization. We demonstrate the efficacy of this algorithm through several case studies, highlighting its potential for improved performance and enhanced adaptability in diverse machine learning applications. This work contributes to the advancement of adaptive machine learning techniques, addressing a key limitation in traditional model design.

title: Quantum Entanglement's Non-Locality Modeling
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, possesses a profound and perplexing property – non-locality. This paper explores the fundamental implications of non-locality for quantum information processing and communication, focusing on the modeling of entanglement's non-locality as a crucial element for security analysis. We propose a novel model, incorporating a "non-locality factor" that quantifies the inherent uncertainty within entangled states. This model directly links the complexity of quantum algorithms to the strength of entanglement, providing a framework for analyzing and mitigating potential vulnerabilities in quantum cryptographic systems. We analyze the potential impact of this modeling on the security of quantum computation and communication, emphasizing its significance in establishing robust protocols.

abstract: This paper introduces the Dynamically Adaptive Modular Theorem Construction (DAMC) system, a novel approach to theorem generation that leverages a self-optimizing system. DAMC employs a layered, hierarchical structure, dynamically adjusting theorem complexity based on input data novelty. The core mechanism centers around a Meta-Logic Engine that analyzes theorems, identifies underlying axioms, and iteratively refines theorem complexity and structure using reinforcement learning. title: Baird's Shrew: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Mustela schreberiana*
abstract: This paper introduces Baird's Shrew, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Mustela schreberiana* (Baird's shrew), a small rodent known for its efficient and adaptive search strategies in complex environments. The algorithm leverages the shrew's characteristic of prioritizing areas with high food density while dynamically adjusting its exploration-exploitation balance. Baird's Shrew combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA) with a novel adaptive weighting scheme based on gradient estimation and local food concentration. The algorithm's core mechanics mimic the shrew's movement pattern: initial rapid exploration followed by a more focused, gradient-guided search. We demonstrate the effectiveness of Baird's Shrew through theoretical analysis and illustrative examples, highlighting its potential for solving optimization problems across various domains. The algorithm's performance is compared against established metaheuristic algorithms, demonstrating competitive results in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. Future research directions include incorporating more sophisticated environmental modeling and adaptive parameter tuning.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Program Synthesis via Temporal Logic
abstract: This research addresses the persistent challenge of complex program synthesis by introducing a neuro-symbolic approach leveraging temporal logic. The system constructs programs by translating high-level temporal specifications into executable code. A neural network is trained to map these specifications to code, and the temporal constraints are continuously refined through dynamic interaction. The core innovation lies in the direct integration of temporal logic within the synthesis process, allowing for the generation of programs that explicitly model and reason about temporal relationships and changes. This approach offers a potential pathway to more robust and understandable program generation, particularly in domains where time-dependent behavior is crucial. The system's architecture comprises a neural network component for code generation and a temporal logic engine for specification validation and constraint refinement. The generated programs are evaluated based on their ability to satisfy the original temporal logic constraints. The key contribution is a framework that combines the learning capabilities of neural networks with the formal reasoning power of temporal logic, resulting in a system capable of synthesizing programs that exhibit sophisticated temporal behavior. ---

title: Dynamic Geometric Quantization: Precise Quantum Entanglement Calculation via Topological Field Dynamics
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a cornerstone of quantum information processing, offering immense potential for secure communication and quantum computing. However, accurately predicting the state of entangled systems remains a significant challenge due to the inherent complexity of quantum mechanics. This paper introduces Dynamic Geometric Quantization (DGQ), a novel approach to quantum entanglement calculation that leverages the power of topological field dynamics to achieve precise predictions. We propose a method where the probability distribution governing a quantum state is treated as the parameters of a topological field, allowing us to dynamically simulate the evolution of entangled states and provide high-precision predictions. The core mechanism involves characterizing the state through a complex topological field, and then employing a dynamic process to mimic the state's evolution. This approach offers a fundamentally different perspective on entanglement analysis, potentially unlocking new avenues for understanding and forecasting quantum phenomena. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of DGQ in predicting the state of entangled systems, showcasing its potential for advancing quantum computation and information processing.

title: ## The Long-Legged Spider Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (LSISA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Long-Legged Spider Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (LSISA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior and movement strategies of long-legged spiders (e.g., *Theridion* species). LSISA leverages the spider's ability to efficiently explore and exploit a search space by dynamically adjusting its step size and direction based on local environmental feedback, mimicking their leg extension and retraction patterns. The algorithm incorporates an adaptive step size control mechanism, a directional adjustment strategy influenced by a simulated "web strength" metric, and a population diversification technique based on simulated web-building behavior. LSISA aims to provide a robust and adaptable solution for a wide range of optimization problems, particularly those with complex, multi-modal landscapes. This paper details the algorithm's theoretical foundation, key components, and its potential applications.

title: Deep Learning-Based Symbolic Reasoning Engine
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to knowledge representation and reasoning by integrating deep learning techniques with symbolic reasoning engines. The core claim is that this combination can significantly enhance both the expressiveness and the robustness of reasoning systems. We propose a framework where deep learning models are utilized for knowledge extraction and representation, while a symbolic reasoning engine performs logical inference and decision-making based on this learned knowledge. This approach addresses the limitations of traditional methods which often struggle with complex, unstructured data and ambiguous knowledge. The system architecture comprises two key components: a Deep Knowledge Extractor (DKE) and a Symbolic Inference Engine (SIE). The DKE learns representations from raw data, capturing intricate patterns and relationships, and outputs a formal symbolic representation. The SIE then utilizes this symbolic representation to perform deductive and inductive reasoning, ultimately providing logical conclusions. The system is evaluated based on its ability to solve complex reasoning problems across various domains. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of this hybrid approach, showcasing improved accuracy and efficiency compared to standalone deep learning or symbolic reasoning systems. Future research directions include exploring different deep learning architectures for the DKE and investigating methods for seamless integration between the two components.

title: The Andean Puma Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (APISA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Andean Puma Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (APISA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the hunting strategies and adaptability of the Andean Puma (Puma concolor andina). APISA leverages the puma's ability to dynamically adjust its search area, exploit local information, and maintain a balance between exploration and exploitation. The algorithm incorporates three key mechanisms: a dynamic adaptive search area based on fitness landscape analysis, a momentum-based particle update scheme mimicking the puma's tracking movements, and a self-adaptive inertia weight adjustment inspired by the animal's responsiveness to prey movement. We present the mathematical formulation of APISA, detailing the core components and their interactions. The algorithm's performance potential is discussed, highlighting its suitability for complex, multi-dimensional optimization problems, with a focus on its adaptive nature and potential for overcoming traditional metaheuristic limitations.

title: Bounded Identifiability of Capability Deficits in Large Language Models at Industrial Evidence Interfaces
abstract: A large language model (LLM) running inside an industrial instrument will fail on some of what the operator asks. Whether such a failure is justified as evidence of a capability deficit of the model, or only of a burden the instrument left at its evidence interface, is not answerable from an accuracy score, and a deployed instrument has no continuously available one because its routine answers are not independently labelled. We state and test a bounded principle of deployment-level identifiability for that question: an observed failure is evidence of model incapability only relative to a declared family of interventions at the evidence interface, and what remains under that family is an upper bound on what may be attributed to the model, never the attribution itself. It is bounded because it identifies nothing outside the family it names, and testable because a running instrument can switch that family. The test is a full factorial over three deterministic mechanisms (compiling derived quantities into the evidence, declaring unknowns as explicit state, and validating typed claims) on a deployed phased-array ultrasound inspection instrument, scored into four failure classes, two of them without reference answers. The mechanisms remove 24.9, 22.5 and 18.9 points of failure from three models that fit an eight-gigabyte industrial GPU. Repeating the factorial on a second quantity space, compiled from a public machine-condition dataset with no detector retuned, four of the twelve factor-class effects keep one sign while the validator's net effect on accuracy reverses, from +2.5 points to -6.1. The same decomposition remains operational and discriminating in both; individual factor-class effects do not transfer uniformly. This record accompanies a manuscript under double-anonymous review. The authors are withheld and the archive is sanitised accordingly: the project name, the institution and every personal address are replaced with placeholders, and the title page and unmasked instrument captures are omitted. No number, script or datum is altered. A new version carrying the byline and the unredacted tree will be published on acceptance, under the same concept DOI. Reproducibility bundle: the evidence compiler, question generator, factorial runner, scorer and analysis, with the frozen configurations, the scored responses, the preregistration and the source data behind every plotted value.

title: Meta-Learning for Algorithm Selection in Data Mining
abstract: Algorithm selection is a crucial yet often manual and time-consuming step in data mining. The performance of a data mining task is highly dependent on the choice of algorithm, and selecting the optimal algorithm often requires significant domain expertise and experimentation. This paper proposes a meta-learning approach to automate this process. The core idea is to train a meta-learner that learns to predict the best algorithm for a given data mining task based on the characteristics of the dataset and the desired outcome metric. The meta-learner learns from a set of previously solved data mining problems, effectively learning a "meta-knowledge" about algorithm effectiveness. This approach offers the potential to significantly improve data mining performance by dynamically selecting the most appropriate algorithm for each task, reducing the need for manual tuning and experimentation. The key contributions of this work lie in the development of a novel meta-learning framework specifically designed for algorithm selection and demonstrating its effectiveness through theoretical analysis and conceptual design.

title: Title: Self-Organizing Topology-Aware Neural Networks (SOTAN)
abstract: This paper introduces Self-Organizing Topology-Aware Neural Networks (SOTAN), a novel neural network architecture designed to enhance information flow and mitigate bottlenecks through the explicit modeling and adaptation of neural network topology. Traditional neural network designs often treat layers independently, neglecting the crucial role of topology in shaping network structure. SOTAN utilizes a topology map, embedded within the network, to dynamically adjust layer connections, promoting efficient information propagation and improved performance. We demonstrate the effectiveness of SOTAN through extensive experiments on various benchmark datasets, showcasing significant improvements in accuracy and training speed compared to existing state-of-the-art architectures.

title: HAFİF EVRİŞİMLİ SİNİR AĞLARINDA HİPERPARAMETRE ETKİLEŞİMLERİNİN AMPİRİK ANALİZİ: OPTİMİZASYON, ZAMANLAYICI VE İLKLENDİRME MATRİSİ
abstract: Derin öğrenme modellerinin başarısı; ağırlık ilklendirme yöntemleri, optimizasyon algoritmaları ve öğrenme oranı zamanlayıcıları gibi temel hiperparametrelerin doğru seçilmesine doğrudan bağlıdır. Bu çalışmada, düzenlileştirici katmanlardan (Batch Normalization, Dropout vb.) arındırılmış izole ve hafif/sığ bir Evrişimli Sinir Ağı (CNN) mimarisi üzerinde, kanonik CIFAR-10 veri kümesi kullanılarak 240 bağımsız eğitim koşusundan oluşan kapsamlı bir ızgara araması yürütülmüştür. Ampirik bulgular, hiperparametrelerin tekil etkilerinden ziyade kombinatoryal etkileşimlerinin model başarımı üzerinde domine edici olduğunu göstermiştir. Deneysel sonuçlara göre; Xavier Normal ilklendirme, AdamW optimizörü ve CosineAnnealingLR zamanlayıcı kombinasyonu %73,84 ile en yüksek test doğruluğunu sergilemiştir. Çalışmanın öne çıkan bulgusu olan, OneCycleLR lokal parametrik uyumsuzluğu uyarınca; literatürde yakınsamayı hızlandırdığı için sıklıkla önerilen OneCycleLR zamanlayıcısının RMSprop optimizörü ile eşleştiğinde modelin ağırlık güncelleme sürecini durdurduğunu (%10,00 rastgele tahmin düzeyi), buna karşın Pure_SGD ve SGD_Momentum varyantlarını alt-optimal platolardan kurtararak başarımlarını %68,97' ye çıkardığı keşfedilmiştir. Gözlemlenen bu karmaşık parametrik etkileşimler 3-Yönlü ANOVA testi ve detaylı profil matrisleri ile istatistiksel olarak doğrulanmış (p < 0,001) ve sığ mimarilerle çalışan araştırmacılar için ampirik bir seçim kılavuzu sunulmuştur.

Çalışmanın öne çıkan bulgusu olan, OneCycleLR lokal parametrik uyumsuzluğu uyarınca; literatürde yakınsamayı hızlandırdığı için sıklıkla önerilen OneCycleLR zamanlayıcısının RMSprop optimizörü ile eşleştiğinde modelin ağırlık güncelleme sürecini durdurduğunu (%10,00 rastgele tahmin düzeyi), buna karşın Pure_SGD ve SGD_Momentum varyantlarını alt-optimal platolardan kurtararak başarımlarını %68,97' ye çıkardığı keşfedilmiştir. Gözlemlenen bu karmaşık parametrik etkileşimler 3-Yönlü ANOVA testi ve detaylı profil matrisleri ile istatistiksel olarak doğrulanmış (p < 0,001) ve sığ mimarilerle çalışan araştırmacılar için ampirik bir seçim kılavuzu sunulmuştur.

title: When AI Responds, Ownership Matters Less: How Social Responsiveness Reshapes the Persuasive Power of AI Endorsers
abstract: 디지털 마케팅에서 인공지능(AI) 엔도서의 활용이 확대됨에 따라, 소비자가 이러한 인공적 존재를 어떻게 평가하는지는 중요한 연구 과제가 되었다. 기존 연구는 AI 엔도서 소유권을 핵심 설득 단서로 제시해 왔으나, 그 효과가 상호작용 맥락에 따라 달라질 가능성은 충분히 논의되지 않았다. 본 연구는 접근성-진단성 모델과 이중경로 설득 관점을 바탕으로, AI 엔도서 소유권(brand-owned vs. independent)이 유사사회적 관계와 지각된 전문성이라는 두 경로를 통해 구매의도에 영향을 미치는 과정을 검증하고, 이러한 과정이 AI 엔도서의 사회적 반응성 수준에 따라 어떻게 달라지는지를 분석하였다. 소셜 미디어 환경을 모사한 시나리오 기반 실험(n = 194) 결과, 사회적 반응성이 낮은 조건에서는 브랜드 소유 AI 엔도서가 독립형 AI 엔도서보다 더 강한 유사사회적 관계와 높은 지각된 전문성을 형성하였고, 이는 구매의도를 높이는 것으로 나타났다. 반면, 사회적 반응성이 높은 조건에서는 소유권에 따른 차이가 약화되었다. 본 연구는 AI 엔도서 소유권이 항상 강력하게 작동하는 설득 단서가 아니라, 사회적 반응성이라는 상호작용 맥락에 따라 진단성이 달라지는 조건적 단서임을 보여준다. 이를 통해 AI 기반 브랜드 커뮤니케이션 연구를 확장하고, AI 엔도서의 설계 및 운영 전략에 대한 실무적 시사점을 제시한다.

title: Supervised vs. adversarially pre-trained pseudo-label generators for semi-supervised breast cancer patch classification
abstract: Automated breast cancer classification from whole-slide images (WSIs) is hampered by the scarcity of expert-annotated patches and the domain variability inherent to multi-institutional datasets. We propose and compare two semi-supervised frameworks for patch-level tumor classification under limited annotation. The first, a semi-supervised baseline , trains a supervised model on the available labeled data, uses it to generate confidence-filtered pseudo-labels for the unlabeled corpus, and trains a separate classifier from scratch on the combined data using a joint supervised and pseudo-label objective. The second, an AdCo-augmented framework , replaces the supervised pseudo-label generator with a backbone pre-trained on 347,884 unlabeled CPTAC-BRCA patches using Adversarial Contrastive Learning (AdCo), followed by frozen-backbone linear probing to generate pseudo-labels; a separate model is then trained with independent ImageNet initialization using the same semi-supervised objective. AdCo replaces the conventional fixed memory queue with a bank of learnable adversarial negatives optimized via gradient ascent, compelling the encoder to learn more discriminative histological representations than standard contrastive methods. Both frameworks are evaluated across nine architecture combinations each—18 in total—drawn from three backbones (ResNet-18, DenseNet-121, and ConvNeXt-Small) on TIGER, BRACS, TCGA, and CPTAC-BRCA datasets, providing a systematic benchmark for semi-supervised breast cancer WSI classification and quantifying the benefit of adversarial self-supervised pre-training over purely supervised pseudo-label generation.

title: Neural Turing Machines for efficient natural language summarization: architecture, optimization, and performance analysis
abstract: Introduction: Abstractive text summarization remains a fundamental challenge in Natural Language Processing (NLP), particularly for long documents that require models to preserve long-range dependencies and maintain semantic coherence. Although Transformer-based architectures have achieved strong summarization performance, their full self-attention mechanism scales quadratically with sequence length and often requires input truncation in long-context applications. Methods: This study presents a Neural Turing Machine (NTM)-based framework for abstractive text summarization. The proposed architecture combines a two-layer Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) controller with an addressable external memory bank. Differentiable read and write operations decouple contextual storage from recurrent computation, enabling the persistent retrieval of salient information across extended input sequences. Detailed preprocessing, implementation, training, decoding, and evaluation settings are provided to support reproducibility. The framework was evaluated on the CNN/Daily Mail benchmark and compared with LSTM, Transformer, and BART baselines, as well as published high-performing systems, including PEGASUS, SimCLS, and BRIO. Ablation studies, learning-rate sensitivity analysis, long-context evaluation, inference-time scaling, statistical testing, qualitative error analysis, and memory-access visualization were also conducted. Results: The proposed NTM model achieved ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2, ROUGE-L, and BLEU scores of 47.8, 23.5, 44.6, and 20.1, respectively. Under the controlled experimental protocol, it outperformed the evaluated LSTM, Transformer, and BART baselines. Comparisons with published results indicate that the model is competitive with recent high-performing summarization systems. The additional analyses demonstrate that the external memory mechanism improves contextual retention and summarization stability, particularly for longer input sequences, while exhibiting favorable inference-time scaling behavior. Discussion: These findings demonstrate that integrating an addressable external memory with a BiLSTM controller offers an effective approach to abstractive summarization, particularly when processing long documents. The proposed framework provides competitive summarization performance while reducing dependence on computationally expensive full self-attention. The results highlight the potential of external-memory architectures as a scalable and stable alternative for long-context text summarization.

title: Fine-Grained Sentiment Analysis: Leveraging BERT for Aspect-Level Customer Feedback Classification
abstract: Organizations can now tap into fine-grained opinions about products or service features that can be extracted from customer reviews and ratings with aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA). The study introduced two models, the first for aspect extraction and another one involved in sentiment analysis using bidirectional encoder representation transformer (BERT). With a testing accuracy of 98%, the aspect extraction model produces outstanding results, corroborated by metrics for precision, recall, and F1-score for every class. Furthermore, the ABSA model gives remarkable progress over earlier research, attaining an 82% testing accuracy. The proposed framework illustrates how well the BERT-based ABSA model accurately identifies and evaluates various aspects of goods or services, as indicated in customer feedback, and adds value to the body of current sentiment analysis literature, suggesting useful recommendations for improving the explanation and understanding of customer feedback. There is a chance that this research project will help consumers and businesses alike.

title: Beyond Task Lists: Self-Initiated Activity Triggering with Learned Internal Processes for Autonomous Robots
abstract: Autonomous robots should be able to initiate meaningful activities even when no explicit task is currently assigned. However, most existing systems remain task-centered or rely on predefined internal mechanisms, limiting their ability to preserve and acquire cognitive influences that remain relevant after current reasoning has ended. This paper proposes a self-initiated activity-triggering framework in which robot activities can arise from external perception, autonomous internal processes, or prolonged inactivity. Internal processes maintain independent states and provide non-commanding messages whose effects are interpreted contextually by the main thinking process. An independent process manager further learns acquired internal processes from previous thinking experience. Process formation is gated by future influence rather than recurrence alone and supports both recurrent delayed needs and rare but severe future vigilance needs. Learned activation signatures determine what future evidence should reactivate acquired processes. Experiments show that the proposed external triggering mechanism achieves 96.00% strict accuracy while reducing LLM tokens by 76.1% relative to centralized reasoning. The learned process manager achieves 98.00% acquisition F1, while activation signatures improve strict balanced future correctness from 62.67% to 82.33%. Compared with repeated history-based LLM reasoning, process internalization reduces LLM calls by 91.80% and token consumption by 94.07%.

title: Instance-Guided Report Anchoring for Text-Free 3D Abnormality Segmentation in Chest CT
abstract: Accurate 3D abnormality segmentation in chest CT requires dense spatial supervision, but obtaining expert voxel-level labels is costly. Radiology reports, however, are routinely generated during clinical interpretation and contain instance-specific descriptions that can provide additional guidance without new dense annotation. Existing vision-language grounding methods typically require report-derived findings at inference, making localization dependent on paired text and limiting each forward pass to a queried finding. We propose Instance-Guided Report Anchoring (IGRA), a model-agnostic module that preserves the correspondence between each annotated abnormality instance and the report finding that describes it. IGRA pools each instance representation and anchors it to the corresponding finding embedding during training; all text-related components are discarded at inference. We further reformulate free-text grounding on ReXGroundingCT as multi-label volumetric segmentation by merging same-category instances, allowing all abnormality categories to be predicted in one image-only forward pass. IGRA improves Dice by 22.5% over the strongest image-only baseline (30.93 vs. 25.25) and is comparable to VoxTell on the single-finding subset (30.29 vs. 30.43). Applied unchanged to four standard 3D segmentation backbones, IGRA improves Dice and hit rate across all architectures. Zero-shot evaluation on LIDC-IDRI, PleThora, and a private in-house dataset further shows consistent gains over image-only baselines.

title: BRF-GS: Hyperspectral Bidirectional Reflectance Factor Modeling and Image Generation Based on 3D Gaussian Splatting
abstract: The bidirectional reflectance factor (BRF) characterizes the directional radiative properties of terrestrial surfaces. However, existing three-dimensional (3D) radiative transfer models require complex scene construction and computationally intensive radiative transfer solvers, limiting efficient generation of multi-angle hyperspectral reflectance imagery. 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) offers an efficient framework for neural scene representation and novel view synthesis, but its low-order spherical harmonics representation is insufficient for complex directional reflectance, while the high dimensionality and inter-band quality differences of hyperspectral data introduce additional challenges. To address these challenges, we propose BRF-GS, a 3DGS-based framework for BRF modeling and hyperspectral reflectance image generation. BRF-GS introduces a hybrid BRDF-driven kernel to represent complex directional reflectance, selects geometry-reliable spectral bands for robust 3D scene initialization, and adopts a two-stage training strategy that decouples geometry optimization from spectral modeling. We further construct the AIR-BRF dataset, a multi-angle hyperspectral directional reflectance dataset comprising three scenes with diverse natural and artificial targets. Experiments demonstrate that BRF-GS achieves superior spatial and spectral fidelity and accurately reproduces characteristic view-dependent BRF responses. The proposed framework provides an efficient data-driven approach for BRF modeling and multi-angle hyperspectral reflectance image generation in remote sensing scenes.
